steps.what: Bring the payment terminal or receive cash at the table.
Select the table check and enter the requested payment amount.
Collect payments and help customers with cash or declined tenders.
Check payment confirmation and close the paid table balance.

tasks.design: Test native table-check and terminal synchronization in the {OTHER} restaurant point-of-sale system. Carry the requested amount and payment confirmation between screens while keeping terminal delivery, cash handling and customer assistance with the waiter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Table checks and terminal entries may be separate.
tasks.enabler_now: Native payment integration can carry check references and settlement status.
tasks.still_hard: Split bills, cash and declined tenders need attention.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve a disputed split without making guests feel rushed.
tasks.altitude: Less payment re-entry, with unchanged authority over discounts and disputed bills.

reach.task: Explain payment arrangements to a large party.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: integrated terminal workflows can reduce repeated amount entry and closure checks; this does not replace cash service.

assumptions: Boundary starts with a prepared check and ends with payment closure, excluding check creation. Customer tender time and existing authorization runtime remain outside the focal baseline and unchanged.

Restaurant system supplies table_id, check_id, version, balance and currency; terminal supplies transaction_id, check_reference, paid_amount and status. Missing integration retains manual checks; no card credential extraction.
Native configuration first. Guests are not required to adopt self-payment, so no transferred guest work is claimed as saving.
unknowns: Terminal compatibility, cash share and split-bill volume.
research_questions: Does synchronization prevent closure against a declined or partial payment?

already_counted.description: Check payment results and table closure.

incremental.description: Report mismatched check references and status failures.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=80 gross=20 net=19 after 1 upkeep. Low: mostly cash or existing integration; high: supported terminals. All walking, cash handling and guest assistance remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record food orders and transmit them to kitchen staff.

steps.what: Clarify patrons food and beverage choices and special requests.
Write order slips or enter food orders with seat and modifier details.
Transmit recorded orders to the kitchen and clarify special instructions.

tasks.design: Test the {OTHER} restaurant point-of-sale handheld order form and native kitchen routing. The waiter selects dishes and structured modifiers, checks kitchen order v1 before sending, and personally clarifies unusual preparation or allergy instructions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper or memorized orders must be entered again at a fixed terminal.
tasks.enabler_now: Native handheld order capture and kitchen routing avoid the second transcription.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous modifiers and allergy handling require communication with kitchen staff.
tasks.human_edge: Detect when a modifier does not express what the guest actually requested.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate order writing; responsibility for accurate guest requests stays unchanged.

reach.task: Identify unclear modifiers before preparation starts.
reach.learn: Kitchen routing, modifier limits and allergy escalation.

evidence.claim: Lightspeed Order Anywhere routes orders through a restaurant point-of-sale system to the kitchen or bar; the digest supports routing capability rather than a waiter time-saving number.
Model knowledge: handheld capture can reduce repeated writing while leaving special-instruction clarification with staff.

assumptions: Boundary includes capturing and sending orders, not food preparation. Clarifying table choices is shared with the separate taking-orders task; roll-ups must resolve that common action once.

Menu owner supplies item_id, item_name, available_state and allowed_modifier_ids; waiter supplies table_id, seat, quantity and special_instruction. Missing codes or network access retain paper entry and verbal kitchen confirmation; no speech extraction is assumed.

Test native capture and routing before code. Approval in s3 checks the exact kitchen order v1, including all modifiers and allergy instructions; edits require another check. The retained half of s3 covers this review and unusual verbal clarification.
unknowns: Paper versus handheld usage and kitchen routing compatibility.
research_questions: Do structured modifiers convey guest intent correctly to kitchen staff?

already_counted.description: Check final kitchen order and clarify unusual requests.

incremental.description: Report missing modifiers and resolve failed transmissions.
Maintain menu codes and kitchen routing.

approvals.approved_version: kitchen order v1 with table, seats, item quantities, modifiers and special instructions; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=40+21+12.5=73.5 gross=26.5 net=24.5 after 2 upkeep. Low: handheld entry already standard; high: substantial repeated entry removed. Guest clarification remains fully counted and shared action cannot be summed twice.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take food and beverage orders from patrons.

steps.what: Clarify patrons food and beverage choices and special requests.
Read back food orders and confirm quantities and dietary requests with patrons.

tasks.design: Keep the conversation and order readback with the waiter. Use the current menu from the {OTHER} restaurant point-of-sale system as a factual reference, without assuming that guest interaction disappears.
tasks.previous_blocker: The core work is understanding spoken choices and constraints.
tasks.enabler_now: No technology change is required for this retained interaction.
tasks.still_hard: Dietary requests, uncertainty and changing guest preferences.
tasks.human_edge: Notice hesitation and make it easy for guests to correct a misunderstanding.

ambition.what: Offer unhurried verbal ordering to guests who cannot use a digital menu.

tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; direct guest attention remains central.

reach.task: Explain ordering assistance to guests on arrival.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: retaining verbal choice clarification and readback preserves guest service; no labour saving is asserted.

assumptions: Boundary is guest conversation, excluding subsequent order recording and kitchen transmission. The shared clarification action must be owned once across the overlapping O*NET tasks.

Menu owner provides dated item names, availability and preparation limits on the existing menu; guests provide choices and dietary requests verbally. Missing menu facts require kitchen clarification. No new structured interface or extraction is needed.
Native menu availability is checked before any code proposal. Zero upkeep is justified because this design adds no system or transferred work.
unknowns: Guest accessibility needs and menu clarification frequency.
research_questions: Which misunderstandings are best prevented by a clearer readback?

incremental.description: No new system or maintenance work is introduced.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 upkeep=0 net=0. Both simple drink orders and complex dietary requests retain the whole conversation; no writing saving is counted here.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare itemized meal checks with applicable taxes.

steps.what: Select the table items, split allocations and approved discounts for the check.
Itemize meal costs and calculate totals and sales taxes using configured codes.
Review the itemized check and release it for presentation to the guest.

tasks.design: Test native table, seat and split-check presets in the {OTHER} restaurant point-of-sale system. Existing tax arithmetic stays in the system, while the waiter checks that meal check v1 reflects consumed items and the agreed split before releasing it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual item selection and split allocation can be repetitive even when totals are already automatic.
tasks.enabler_now: Native seat allocation and check presets reduce selection steps.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed consumption, discretionary discounts and unusual tax classifications.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve who is paying for which items fairly.
tasks.altitude: Less split allocation work; tax policy and discount authority stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Seat allocation and approved adjustment controls.

evidence.claim: Lightspeed Order Anywhere supports restaurant ordering and payment through the point-of-sale system; this supports native check workflows, not a new saving from existing arithmetic.
Model knowledge: native split presets can shorten item allocation while retaining waiter check review.

assumptions: Boundary ends at a ready check and excludes presentation and payment collection. System calculation has 30 workflow units but no human baseline; focal B=70.

Restaurant system supplies table_id, seat, item_id, quantity and posted_price; finance supplies dated item tax codes; waiter supplies split allocation and authorized discounts. Missing or disputed records require manual review and finance referral for tax codes.
Native configuration first. No tax rate is inferred or changed by a model. Approval binds check v1 item lines, allocations, prices, discounts and tax-code snapshot; edits void release.
unknowns: Existing seat allocation and time spent selecting split lines.
research_questions: Do presets reduce allocation work while preserving correct totals across split and partial checks?

already_counted.description: Review the exact check before release.

incremental.description: Report incorrect check presets and investigate new allocation errors.
Maintain finance-approved tax and split settings.

approvals.approved_version: meal check v1: lines, allocations, prices, discounts and tax-code snapshot; edits void release

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=70 R=50 gross=28.571 net=27.571 after 1 upkeep. Low: presets already used; high: repeated split allocation. Existing system tax calculation earns zero labour saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeated order and payment entry while retaining attentive table service and accurate readbacks.
role.ambitious_version: A waiter who spends more time helping guests and less time moving the same order between screens.
